name: Windows — Service Installed with Suspicious Image Path
description:
Attacker objective
Install a new Windows service whose image is a command interpreter, script, or a binary in a user-writable path — for persistence or remote code execution.

Attack logic
Legitimate services run vendor executables from Program Files/System32. A service configured to launch cmd/powershell, a scripting host, an encoded command, or a binary under Temp/AppData is a persistence or lateral-execution mechanism (also used by PsExec-style tools).

Why this detection works
Service-installation auditing (4697) records the service image path; matching interpreter/encoded/user-writable-path patterns isolates malicious services, independent of case.

False positives
A poorly packaged legitimate service that runs a script (rare in a managed estate).

Tuning
Allowlist verified service names/paths; correlate with the installing account and source host.

Required telemetry
Windows Security 4697 (ServiceName, ServiceFileName).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Review the service name, image path and installing account.
2. A shell/encoded/temp-path service is persistence or remote execution — isolate and remove if unauthorised.
3. Correlate with a network logon (PsExec-style lateral) or preceding compromise.
false_positives: A poorly packaged legitimate service that runs a script (rare in a managed estate).
query:
FROM logs-system.security-* METADATA _id, _index, _version
| WHERE event.code == "4697" AND winlog.event_data.ServiceFileName IS NOT NULL
| EVAL svc = TO_LOWER(winlog.event_data.ServiceFileName)
| WHERE svc LIKE "*cmd.exe*" OR svc LIKE "*powershell*" OR svc LIKE "*pwsh*" OR svc LIKE "*rundll32*" OR svc LIKE "*regsvr32*" OR svc LIKE "*mshta*" OR svc LIKE "*cscript*" OR svc LIKE "*wscript*" OR svc LIKE "*windows*temp*" OR svc LIKE "*appdata*" OR svc LIKE "*-enc*" OR svc LIKE "*frombase64*" OR svc LIKE "*downloadstring*" OR svc LIKE "*comspec*"
| KEEP @timestamp, host.name, winlog.event_data.ServiceName, winlog.event_data.ServiceFileName, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName
